# Terra & Form — extended context

> Architecture and interior design studio in Bangkok, Thailand. Website available in French, English and Thai. Contact: contact@terra-and-form.com

## About

Terra & Form designs new-build residences, renovations and extensions, interiors, commercial fit-outs and brand identities in Bangkok. The practice is contextual: site, climate and materials always come before form.

## Services

- Studies, plans & permits: feasibility studies, tailored plans, building permits and regulatory coordination.
- Bespoke residences & homes: design and construction of new residential projects, villas and contemporary custom homes.
- Renovations & extensions: renovations, extensions and additions designed for the place and its uses.
- Interiors, commerce & identity: interior design, commercial fit-outs and visual brand identity development.

## Process

1. Framing — site, brief, budget and schedule are clarified.
2. Design — a spatial, material and sensory direction emerges.
3. Development — plans, visualisations, details and finish choices make the project tangible.
4. Delivery — coordination, site follow-up and quality control through to handover.

## Frequently asked questions

### What kind of projects does Terra & Form take on?

We take on new-build residential projects, renovations and extensions, as well as interior design, commercial fit-outs and brand identity work. See our Services page for more detail.

### Where do you work?

The studio is based in Bangkok and works mainly in the city and its surrounding area. For a project elsewhere in Thailand, get in touch: we review every enquiry individually.

### What does the process look like, step by step?

Every project follows four stages: framing (site, brief, budget, timeline), design (spatial and material direction), development (drawings, details, visualisations) and delivery (coordination and site follow-up through to handover).

### How long does a project take?

It depends heavily on scope. An interior fit-out can be designed in a few weeks, while a new residence or a major renovation takes several months, permits included. We give you a precise estimate after our first conversation.

### What budget should I plan for?

Budget varies with the type, size and finish level of the project. We discuss it openly from the framing stage onward, to build a proposal that matches your means.

### Do I need a building permit?

For new construction or a major renovation in Thailand, a permit is generally required. We handle the regulatory studies and coordination with the relevant authorities on your behalf.

### What happens during the first conversation?

You tell us about your project through the contact form; we reply within 48 working hours to set up a first conversation and understand your needs, your site and what you have in mind.

### What languages can I use with the studio?

We also work with clients in French and Thai.

### How is my personal data used?

Information submitted through the contact form is used solely to handle your enquiry, in accordance with Thailand's Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). Details are in our privacy policy.

### How can I reach you?

The easiest way is our contact form; you can also email us directly at contact@terra-and-form.com or reach us on LINE.

## Projects

- Skyline Residence — A residence conceived as a vantage point over the city, its wide glazed openings framing the Bangkok skyline from every room. (https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/projet/residence-bangkok/)
- Ladprao Villa — Contemporary villa with pool, clean white volumes softened by timber joinery. (https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/projet/villa-ladprao/)
- Phrom Phong Villa — Entrance framed by timber screens and a dense tropical garden, for an intimate arrival despite the urban setting. (https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/projet/villa-phromphong/)

- Architecture and Food Security (2026-04-08) — Hydroponics, aeroponics, building-integrated vertical farms: how architecture is becoming an active player in urban food security, neighbourhood by neighbourhood. (https://www.terra-and-form.com/en/article/architecture-securite-alimentaire/)

- Thailand: When Tradition Meets Tropical Modernism (2026-08-05) — Stilts, deep roof overhangs, bamboo and raw concrete: how a new generation of Thai practices is reinventing vernacular housing to meet climate and Bangkok's urban density.
